abstract: The Escherichia coli transcription initiation factor σ70 was long believed to dissociate from RNA polymerase after promoter escape, following synthesis of short ~9-11 nt RNAs. However, recent evidence indicates σ70 is retained in elongation complexes (ECs), where it enhances pausing-implying that stochastic or factor-mediated displacement is required for processive elongation. Using fluorescence correlation spectroscopy, we quantified σ70 retention in the presence of elongation factors NusG and NusA, demonstrating that NusG-but not NusA-actively promotes σ70 dissociation. Single-molecule TIRF further revealed that NusG-mediated σ70 dissociation becomes favourable as ECs progress, with lower energy barriers for displacement in later elongation stages. These findings suggest a broader mechanistic paradigm in which elongation factors actively displace initiation factors to regulate transcription-a process that may be conserved across all domains of life.
